dream: The card hummed a high note, then dropped low. I pressed the tired wedge down again, but the wedge was gone, turned into a soft, warm stone. It slid under the Leaning Lid, which refused to rest. I leaned hard against a flat line that felt like a drawing of paper. The air thickened, wet and heavy, pressing from a roof I could not see. The slip, tired and waiting, refused to move. I woke with my hands full of the wedge's memory, pressing harder than before, unsure if the weight was real or just a drawing I had pressed into my own corner.
